text:
## Observations

1. For a fixed left endpoint \(l\), an input interval can be contained only if \(L_i \ge l\), and it is contained exactly when \(r \ge R_i\).
2. Among input intervals with \(L_i \ge l\), the smallest \(R_i\) is the first forbidden right endpoint. If there are no such intervals, \(M+1\) serves as the first forbidden endpoint.
3. Moving \(l\) from right to left adds only the input intervals whose left endpoint equals the new \(l\). For intervals with the same left endpoint, only the smallest right endpoint matters.
4. Each valid pair belongs to exactly one left endpoint, so the counts for individual left endpoints can be added.

## Solution sketch

> For a fixed left endpoint \(l\), an input interval can be contained only if \(L_i \ge l\), and it is contained exactly when \(r \ge R_i\).
>
> Moving \(l\) from right to left adds only the input intervals whose left endpoint equals the new \(l\). For intervals with the same left endpoint, only the smallest right endpoint matters.

1. Read the \(N\) intervals and build a table indexed by left endpoint. Initialize each entry to \(M+1\). For each interval, update the entry at \(L_i\) with the smaller of its current value and \(R_i\). This records exactly the information needed when the sweep reaches \(L_i\).

> Among input intervals with \(L_i \ge l\), the smallest \(R_i\) is the first forbidden right endpoint. If there are no such intervals, \(M+1\) serves as the first forbidden endpoint.

2. Sweep \(l\) from \(M\) down to \(1\). Start the running minimum at \(M+1\) and update it with the table entry at \(l\) before counting. The resulting minimum \(b\) is the first forbidden endpoint because the sweep has now included exactly the intervals with \(L_i \ge l\). The valid right endpoints run from \(l\) through \(b-1\), giving \(b-l\) choices. Every eligible interval has \(R_i \ge L_i \ge l\), so this count is always nonnegative. It is zero when \([l,l]\) appears in the input and equals \(M-l+1\) when no interval is eligible.

> Each valid pair belongs to exactly one left endpoint, so the counts for individual left endpoints can be added.

3. Add each count to a running total and print it after the sweep. If every left endpoint contributes zero, the answer is zero. Building the table takes \(O(N+M)\) time, and the sweep takes \(O(M)\) time. The algorithm uses \(O(M)\) auxiliary space when the input intervals are processed as they are read.

isolation.mechanism: codex exec, fresh ephemeral session, empty temporary working directory, user config and exec rules ignored, read-only sandbox, web search and listed features disabled, credential-like variables removed from the environment
isolation.limits: Codex harness instructions and its own tool descriptions remain in the model context; they cannot be removed. Tool isolation is verified post hoc from the event stream, which contained no tool, command, file or search events.
